title: a post Instagram rejected ends as `failed` -- the slot and its photo are lost, and nothing re-books them
evidence: 1 un-retried post(s) marked failed in the last 24h (newest 10.7h ago): post 333 photo 339 slot 2026-09-20 15:15:13.541039 failed 2026-09-20 16:00:58.718029 reason: instagram: 400 code 9007 (Media ID is not available -- the media is not ready for publishing); backfilled 2026-09-20 from log/scheduled_posting.log (row predates failure_reason). The retry path now exists in-repo (Scheduling::FailedPostRetry, wired into bin/scheduled_posting.sh as `scheduling:retry_failed` with APPLY=1): it re-books the SAME row onto a Growth::PostSlotPlanner slot when the stored failure_reason matches a TRANSIENT class (9007/2207027, timeout, 429, 5xx, connection, url_generation) and writes a `retry#N` marker so one failure can never be re-booked twice. Rows counted here are therefore those the retry would NOT touch or has not yet seen: a policy/permission rejection (deliberate -- re-offering rejected content is not ours to decide), a row with no stored reason, a photo file that is gone, or a repair that stopped running. Rows marked `retry#N` are excluded on purpose: they are booked, not lost. Original failure mode ffe9692 (4x/10s publish retry + persisted reason) still stands -- what lands here survived it.

FIXED 2026-09-21 ops-triage -- the slot is re-booked now, and the fix was verified on live data, not only in specs. ROOT CAUSE: 'failed' is terminal in Scheduling::Post's state machine, index_posts_on_photo_id_and_persona_id is UNIQUE (so no replacement row can exist for the same photo), and nothing in the pipeline ever reads a 'failed' row -- so a rejected post lost its slot AND its paid-for render while the publisher exited 0. FIX: Scheduling::FailedPostRetry (packs/scheduling/app/services/scheduling/) re-books the SAME row onto a Growth::PostSlotPlanner slot when the stored failure_reason matches a TRANSIENT class (9007/2207027, timeout, 429, 5xx, connection reset, url_generation) and stamps failure_reason with 'retry#N' so one failure can never be re-booked twice. A policy/permission rejection, a row with no stored reason, or a photo whose file is gone is deliberately LEFT failed for a human -- re-offering rejected content is not ours to decide. Wired into bin/scheduled_posting.sh as 'scheduling:retry_failed' with APPLY=1 LIMIT=3 ahead of the publisher (NON-FATAL, same shape as the caption/hashtag/salvage repairs); the rake task is dry-run by default. VERIFIED: 10 new examples (spec/services/scheduling/failed_post_retry_spec.rb) and 79 examples green across spec/services/{scheduling,growth}; live dry run printed 'examined=1 requeued=1 posts=[333]'; live APPLY=1 re-booked post 333 and psql reads status=scheduled, scheduled_at=2026-09-26 14:00:00Z, failure_reason='retry#1 re-booked 2026-09-26T14:00:00Z | instagram: 400 code 9007 ...', strategy_name=turbo-one-step (caption/hashtags/photo preserved); probe re-run no longer fires this check. The check is now retry-aware: rows marked 'retry#%' are excluded (booked, not lost) and the evidence names the retry path plus what it will not touch.
